text:
## Season so far

D'Andre Swift is the Bears' lead back, and the role has grown as the year went on. Week 1 against CAR was the high point at 31.9 points (124 yards, 3 TD), but he wasn't a steady producer early. Weeks 2 through 4 gave 10.4, 9.8 and 6.4 points. Week 4 was the floor, with a 35% snap share and no touchdown. Since then he has scored in five straight games, and his snap share has gone 58%, 58%, 86% and 77%. He is at 17.3 PTS/G over 8 games, with 10 rushing TDs and a career high in touchdowns already. The Week 8 night against SEA (27 carries, 69 yards, 3 TD, 26.9 points) was a touchdown-driven score on poor efficiency.

## Usage and efficiency

The workload is strong and the efficiency is poor. He has 143 carries at 3.8 yards per carry and a 32% opportunity share. The passing game barely helps him: 29 targets, 24 catches, 162 yards (5.6 yards per target), a 11% target share and no receiving TD. Receiving is a small part of his value.

Goal-line work is why he scores. He has 36 red-zone carries and 19 goal-line carries on the season, and the last four games show the same pattern:

| | Last 4 | Season |
|---|---|---|
| PTS/G | 20.0 | 17.3 |
| Snap % | 70% | 64% |
| Opportunity share | 35% | 32% |
| Yards per carry | 3.2 | 3.8 |
| Yards per target | 4.6 | 5.6 |
| Red-zone carries | 17 | 36 |
| Goal-line carries | 11 | 19 |

More touches are coming at lower efficiency. The touchdowns are not a fluke: 10 actual against 10.3 expected from where his work came. His scoring matches his usage, so I don't expect a sharp regression. The risk is that a 3.2 yards-per-carry back depends on the Bears staying near the goal line.

## Health and situation

I found no verified injury for Swift in 2026. My searches mostly returned 2025 coverage (a groin issue), which doesn't apply, so I'm not counting it.

The thing to watch is Kyle Monangai, who is listed Questionable with a toe injury. Toe injuries are slow to clear for running backs because they limit pushing off and cutting. Re-aggravation is common, and a first game back usually comes with a limited snap count. Beat-writer coverage this season describes him missing several weeks. I couldn't verify his exact Week 11 status.

He had a 23% opportunity share in the four games he played this year. If he returns, that comes mostly out of Swift's 35% share. Roschon Johnson is the other piece: he had 25 carries over the last four games, a 14% share, and handles some short-yardage work. Zavier Scott and Brittain Brown are on IR. I couldn't confirm any coaching or QB change.

## Outlook

The Bears are on their bye in Week 10, which gives Swift and the whole backfield a free week. The schedule is uneven:
- Week 9 vs TB: tough
- Week 11 vs NO: easy
- Week 12 @ DET: tough
- Week 13 vs JAX: tough

The projection is 136.4 points over 8 games, or 18.9 per game. It includes ×1.05 for the usage trend and ×0.90 for Monangai's return.

**Floor:** a Week 4-style game of about 6 to 8 points if the Bears fall behind or Monangai takes a bigger share. **Ceiling:** 25 or more when he gets goal-line carries, as in Weeks 1 and 8.

**Verdict: hold, and start him every week as an RB1/RB2 in half-PPR.** The touchdown work is real, so I wouldn't sell on regression. I also wouldn't pay a premium for him, because his yards per carry is low and Monangai's return caps the upside. If a rival owner values him as a top-5 back, that is a reasonable sell, but I wouldn't shop him otherwise. Week 11 vs NO (easy) is his best remaining matchup.
